title: Is the committed record the published form of Service build applied, from which the fleet is read?
description: The fleet is fed by Generating's published event Service build applied, but ST-DIS-UC02-R01 says the sweep answers from the committed records alone, with no network and no service to operate. An event relay would be a service to operate. If the committed .stego/state.yaml is the event's durable form, the sweep is its projection, and the record's format version is the event's contract. Nothing raises or relays the event today.

title: Where does the registry declare the compiler range it supports, and which domain checks it?
description: ST-DIS-UC04-R04 lets the compiler pin and the registry pin move apart within a range the registry declares. The registry is Supplying's, and apply is Generating's, so Distributing can state the rule but not check it. Nothing declares or checks such a range today.

title: How does apply refuse a pin past its fail date, or a new pin to a withdrawn digest, when the digest lifecycle is Distributing's?
description: Distributing owns the digest lifecycle and publishes Component digest superseded and Component digest withdrawn. Generating can hear them only through the read model Digest standing, but a command checks only specifications, and a specification reads only its own domain's aggregates. Today no code does any of this. Options: (a) apply's handler reads Digest standing, outside what the model can link; (b) Generating keeps its own aggregate of digest standing, changed by a command that policies send when they hear the two events, and apply checks specifications over it; (c) the refusal moves to a Distributing check that runs before apply. It is also open how the events reach a service checkout: the lifecycle records beside the registry are their durable form, and nothing relays them yet.
